newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SWISS WATCH EXPORTS UP 7.8 PCT IN VALUE IN 1997 H1.
newsitem.headline: SWISS WATCH EXPORTS UP 7.8 PCT IN VALUE IN 1997 H1.

text.p: Exports of Swiss watches rose 7.8 percent in the first half of 1997 to 3.857 billion Swiss francs from 3.577 billion in the 1996 first half, helped by weakness in the Swiss franc against the U.S. dollar, the Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry said.
The increase was also tied to improved business in two major European export markets, Germany and Italy.
Hong Kong was the leading export market, totalling 686 million Swiss francs in the first half, a rise of 6.2 percent.
Exports to the U.S., the second-largest market, also rose sharply by 15.8 percent to 515 million francs.

Exports to third-largest market Japan were down 4.6 percent at 373 million in the first half, while exports to Germany and Italy rose by 10.0 and 10.6 percent, to 305 million and 215 million francs, respectively.
Although the value of exports increased, the number of individual finished watches exported fell by 11 percent to 14.9 million in the 1997 first half from 16.7 in first half 1996.
In value terms, however, exports of finished watches, excluding parts, rose 10.6 percent to 3.443 billion Swiss francs in the first half of 1997 compared with 3.114 billion in the first half of 1996.

"This situation is mainly due to the decline in exports of plastic wristwatches, which fell 25.5 percent, offsetting only only partly a gain in exports of watches made of other materials, namely gold and steel," the Federation said.

It added that export demand for gold watches had picked up again after declining in 1996. Exports of gold watches rose 4.1 percent in volume terms and up 7.6 percent in value terms in the first half of 1997.
Exports of steel watches were also up 10.4 percent in volume terms and 32.8 percent in value terms in the first half.
Exports of bi-metal watches of gold and steel were up 1.4 percent in volume and 7.4 percent in value terms.
Exports of gold-plated watches fell 7.4 percent in volume, and 7.5 percent in value.
Exports of watches made from aluminum and brass fell 3.4 percent in volume and 9.6 percent in value terms.
